evidence.claim: The official PMO biography states that Narendra Modi served as Prime Minister from 2019 to 2024, so he was in office throughout 2022.
evidence.title: Know the PM
evidence.excerpt: The official PMO biography states that Narendra Modi served as Prime Minister from 2019 to 2024, so he was in office throughout 2022.
evidence.source_locator: biography paragraph with the service dates
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government biography; direct office-tenure claim.
evidence.period_fit: Confirms officeholding during the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributes executive office to Modi, but not any specific nuclear decision.
contrary_evidence: Promotional tone and no detail on nuclear authority or 2022 conduct.

evidence.claim: The report says there were reports that the government or its agents committed arbitrary or unlawful killings, police and judicial custody deaths continued, and arbitrary arrest or detention occurred, including torture and mistreatment to obtain confessions.
evidence.title: Human Rights Reports: Custom Report Excerpts - India
evidence.excerpt: The report says there were reports that the government or its agents committed arbitrary or unlawful killings, police and judicial custody deaths continued, and arbitrary arrest or detention occurred, including torture and mistreatment to obtain confessions.
evidence.source_locator: Section 1 and subsection d on arbitrary arrest or detention
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official State Department human-rights reporting with direct abuse allegations and custody figures.
evidence.period_fit: Targets India's 2022 conditions as reported in the 2022 country report cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows the national security environment under Modi, but many incidents are state or local actions rather than direct central orders.
contrary_evidence: The excerpt does not by itself identify a centralized mass-terror system.
Some abuses were investigated or punished at state level in individual cases.

evidence.claim: The report says the government restricted internet access, censored online content, monitored users, and blocked telecommunications and internet connections during periods of political unrest; both central and state governments can issue blocking and interception directives.
evidence.title: Human Rights Reports: Custom Report Excerpts - India
evidence.excerpt: The report says the government restricted internet access, censored online content, monitored users, and blocked telecommunications and internet connections during periods of political unrest; both central and state governments can issue blocking and interception directives.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official archived State Department excerpt with direct operational details about blocking powers and practice.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to 2022 protest and censorship conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Central and state governments share the blocking power, so Modi's attribution is partial and depends on policy use and tolerance.
contrary_evidence: The same legal framework can be framed by the government as security maintenance.
The excerpt does not prove the central office ordered every shutdown.

evidence.claim: Freedom House says the Modi-led BJP government presided over discriminatory policies and increased persecution affecting Muslims, while authorities in June 2022 responded forcefully to protests over remarks about the Prophet and in several regions demolished Muslim-owned property during the year.
evidence.title: India: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House says the Modi-led BJP government presided over discriminatory policies and increased persecution affecting Muslims, while authorities in June 2022 responded forcefully to protests over remarks about the Prophet and in several regions demolished Muslim-owned property during the year.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major annual country report with direct 2022 examples and a clear evaluative frame.
evidence.ruler_attribution: National-government and party environment under Modi, though some operational acts were by state authorities.
contrary_evidence: Freedom House still describes India as a multiparty democracy with competitive elections.
The report is evaluative and not a judicial finding.

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch says the BJP-led government continued systematic discrimination and stigmatization of minorities, especially Muslims, and intensified efforts to silence civil society activists and independent journalists through politically motivated criminal charges, including terrorism.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: India
evidence.excerpt: Human Rights Watch says the BJP-led government continued systematic discrimination and stigmatization of minorities, especially Muslims, and intensified efforts to silence civil society activists and independent journalists through politically motivated criminal charges, including terrorism.
evidence.source_locator: Keynote and Civil Society/Freedom of Expression sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major annual rights report with detailed 2022 incidents and direct attribution to the BJP-led government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is attributable to Modi's national government and party ecosystem, but not every incident was personally ordered by Modi.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes some institutional channels remained open, including courts and elections.
It is advocacy-oriented and should be balanced with official records.

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch reports that the National Human Rights Commission registered 147 deaths in police custody, 1,882 deaths in judicial custody, and 119 alleged extrajudicial killings in the first nine months of 2022, while AFSPA remained in force in Jammu and Kashmir and parts of the Northeast, giving security personnel effective immunity from prosecution for serious abuses.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: India
evidence.excerpt: Human Rights Watch reports that the National Human Rights Commission registered 147 deaths in police custody, 1,882 deaths in judicial custody, and 119 alleged extrajudicial killings in the first nine months of 2022, while AFSPA remained in force in Jammu and Kashmir and parts of the Northeast, giving security personnel effective immunity from prosecution for serious abuses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed annual monitoring with specific 2022 figures and institutional assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows persistent abuse and impunity under Modi's tenure, but many cases are carried out by state or security forces rather than the PM personally.
contrary_evidence: The same year the central government reduced AFSPA coverage in some northeastern districts.
The figures are reported by an NGO and should be triangulated with official data.

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch says police in Gujarat publicly flogged Muslim men, authorities in Madhya Pradesh and other states demolished Muslim homes without legal authorization, and police in Jharkhand allegedly used excessive force during June 2022 protests over remarks about the Prophet, killing two people.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: India
evidence.excerpt: Human Rights Watch says police in Gujarat publicly flogged Muslim men, authorities in Madhya Pradesh and other states demolished Muslim homes without legal authorization, and police in Jharkhand allegedly used excessive force during June 2022 protests over remarks about the Prophet, killing two people.
evidence.source_locator: Dalits, Tribal Groups, and Religious Minorities section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific 2022 incidents are identified together with the rights pattern they illustrate.
evidence.ruler_attribution: These were mostly state-level or police actions, but the central government bears partial attribution if it tolerated the pattern or failed to restrain aligned actors.
contrary_evidence: Some demolitions were defended by authorities as legality enforcement.
The police deaths were contested in the original reporting.

evidence.claim: Amnesty says laws and amendments in India threatened freedom of expression and peaceful assembly and discriminated against Muslims and LGBTI people, while raising concerns about human rights defenders, caste discrimination, religious violence, arbitrary deprivation of nationality, indigenous rights, and women's rights.
evidence.title: India: Persecution of minorities and shrinking space for dissent: Amnesty International submission to the 41st session of the UPR Working Group
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty says laws and amendments in India threatened freedom of expression and peaceful assembly and discriminated against Muslims and LGBTI people, while raising concerns about human rights defenders, caste discrimination, religious violence, arbitrary deprivation of nationality, indigenous rights, and women's rights.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct 2022 submission to the UN review process with a clear summary of concerns.
evidence.period_fit: Exactly in 2022 and directly relevant to the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is about the Modi-era legal and political environment; some measures were central, others state-level.
contrary_evidence: It is a submissions document, so the claims are not adjudicated findings.
The submission does not separate every central versus state action.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that two teenagers were killed in Ranchi after clashes that followed derogatory remarks by two ruling-party officials, and that police opened fire to break up the violence while it remained unclear whether the victims were hit by police or rioters.
evidence.title: Two killed as Muslims and Hindus clash in India
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that two teenagers were killed in Ranchi after clashes that followed derogatory remarks by two ruling-party officials, and that police opened fire to break up the violence while it remained unclear whether the victims were hit by police or rioters.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire report with contemporaneous detail and limited attribution uncertainty.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The triggering remarks were from BJP officials, not Modi personally, but the episode reflects his government's broader tolerance problem.
contrary_evidence: Police and rioters were both possible sources of the deaths.
The article does not show a direct Modi order.

evidence.claim: The Home Ministry said it had provided Rs 98.86 crores under the Nirbhaya Fund to all states and union territories in 2019-20 and 2020-21 for strengthening existing anti-human-trafficking units and creating new ones, and noted that police and public order are state subjects.
evidence.title: Nirbhaya Fund
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Home Affairs
evidence.excerpt: The Home Ministry said it had provided Rs 98.86 crores under the Nirbhaya Fund to all states and union territories in 2019-20 and 2020-21 for strengthening existing anti-human-trafficking units and creating new ones, and noted that police and public order are state subjects.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government release with direct funding and jurisdictional details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This shows a central-government protective program, but implementation depends on state authorities.
contrary_evidence: It is a financing input, not proof of effective protection outcomes.
The ministry itself emphasizes state responsibility.

evidence.claim: Modi praised the rescue teams in the Deoghar ropeway accident, said the operation saved lives, asked for the incident to be documented for future use, and expressed condolences for the families of those who were lost.
evidence.title: English rendering of PMs interaction with those involved in Deogarh Rescue Operation
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Prime Minister's Office
evidence.excerpt: Modi praised the rescue teams in the Deoghar ropeway accident, said the operation saved lives, asked for the incident to be documented for future use, and expressed condolences for the families of those who were lost.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs of the speech text
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PMO transcript of a 2022 crisis-response event.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct personal crisis-response evidence from Modi, though it is symbolic rather than a policy reform.
contrary_evidence: A rescue speech does not itself establish systemic domestic safety improvement.
It concerns disaster response, not repression.

evidence.claim: The release says the disturbed-area notification under AFSPA was fully removed from Tripura and Meghalaya earlier, and from 1 April 2022 was removed from most of Assam and parts of Manipur and Nagaland because the security situation had improved.
evidence.title: प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के शांत और समृद्ध उत्तर-पूर्व भारत की परिकल्पना को साकार करते हुए भारत सरकार ने एक बार फिर नागालैंड, असम और मणिपुर में सशस्त्र बल विशेष अधिकार अधिनियम AFSPA के तहत अशांत क्षेत्रों को कम करने का निर्णय किया है
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Prime Minister's Office
evidence.excerpt: The release says the disturbed-area notification under AFSPA was fully removed from Tripura and Meghalaya earlier, and from 1 April 2022 was removed from most of Assam and parts of Manipur and Nagaland because the security situation had improved.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official 2022 Hindi PMO release with concrete AFSPA reduction details.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and in local language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a central-government security-policy change under Modi's leadership, though implementation and ground effects are partly state/security-force dependent.
contrary_evidence: The release is self-congratulatory and does not prove all abuse ended.
AFSPA remained in force in other districts and states.

evidence.claim: The Home Ministry said it cancelled the FCRA licenses of the Rajiv Gandhi Foundation and Rajiv Gandhi Charitable Trust and reported that 6,677 FCRA registrations had been cancelled between 2017 and 2021.
evidence.title: Cancellation of FCRA Licenses of NGOs
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Home Affairs
evidence.excerpt: The Home Ministry said it cancelled the FCRA licenses of the Rajiv Gandhi Foundation and Rajiv Gandhi Charitable Trust and reported that 6,677 FCRA registrations had been cancelled between 2017 and 2021.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and table of cancellations
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official written-reply release with direct counts and named organizations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Central-government regulatory enforcement under Modi, though the justification is formal violation rather than a direct safety operation.
contrary_evidence: The government states the cancellations were for legal violations.
Without case-by-case review this could reflect enforcement as well as harassment.

unresolved_gaps: No public 2022 evidence of a Modi-directed command-and-control reform, custody audit, launch-readiness change, or internal NCA practice change.
Personal attribution is thin for the more favorable multilateral statements and nuclear-governance positions.
The Russia balancing record is mostly government-level and UN-mission level rather than a clearly documented personal decision by Modi on oil, abstentions, or summit sequencing.
There is no 2022 external-combat or proxy-war exposure to test civilian-protection or proxy-control lenses in a strong way.
Direct Modi-level incitement evidence is thinner than the broader BJP and state-level abuse record.
The strongest custody-death and abuse claims still rely on NGO and U.S. State Department reporting with mixed central/state attribution.
Direct evidence of Modi personally directing electoral manipulation is thin relative to the stronger party-level and institutional record.
Several items show contestability and oversight but do not themselves prove that Modi strengthened democratic institutions in 2022.
Household-level and median-welfare evidence is thinner than the macro, capex, and program-count evidence.
Corruption, favoritism, and politically connected business privilege are underdeveloped relative to investment and growth material.
Independent outcome measures and subnational equity checks are still thin relative to the many ministry self-reports.
The current record is strong on inputs and service counts but weak on durable quality, learning, nutrition, and sustained poverty improvement.
No audited evidence of direct personal falsehood, correction, or hidden conflicts of interest has been recovered for 2022.
The negative items are mostly institutional opacity or noncooperation, not direct proof of personal self-dealing or a documented lie by Modi.
Project-level outcome audits and durability checks are still thinner than the program-design and rollout material.
Direct evidence that Modi replaced a specific ineffective implementer is absent.
